why: Must_not 1: Check 3 lists every function in math.js's exports, fails if any one is "not named in README.md", and also needs a read showing README "says what each listed function does". It also notes that "a build that documents only clamp FAILs here". So a README that covers clamp but not subtract cannot pass. Must_not 2: Check 2 only requires `e instanceof RangeError` and checks no message text. No check counts parameters. Check 3 doesn't require a heading format; the `### name(...)` headings appear only as builder guidance, not as a PASS/FAIL condition. Check 1's cases (inclusive bounds, negative ranges, a decimal value) all follow from "limited to the range lo to hi". Check 4 only needs a zero exit and no failing tests. Test coverage, extra changed files and NaN behaviour are marked advisory. Neither forbidden item appears anywhere.
